title: AWS
subtitle: A VPC with edge, load balancers, private access, storage kinds and connected networks.

boxes.label: S3
boxes.says: S3 stores objects in buckets.
boxes.detail: Classes: Standard, Infrequent Access, Glacier for cold archive. Objects are addressed by key over HTTPS, not mounted as disks.

boxes.label: EBS
boxes.says: EBS is a block disk for one node.
boxes.detail: A volume attaches to one instance in its Availability Zone, like a hard drive. Snapshots back it up to S3.

boxes.label: EFS
boxes.says: EFS is a shared file system.
boxes.detail: NFS mounted by many pods or instances across Availability Zones at once, and it grows as files are added.

boxes.label: EKS
boxes.says: EKS runs the Kubernetes control plane.
boxes.detail: AWS operates the control plane; worker nodes or Fargate run pods. ECS and Lambda are the other compute options.

boxes.label: IAM
boxes.says: IAM roles and policies grant access.
boxes.detail: Policies say who may do what on which resource. IRSA gives each pod its own role instead of long-lived keys.

boxes.label: CloudWatch
boxes.says: CloudWatch collects metrics, logs and alarms.
boxes.detail: Alarms on metrics such as 5XX count or latency notify operators or trigger scaling.

boxes.label: VPC
boxes.says: A VPC is your private network.
boxes.detail: A CIDR range split into public and private subnets per Availability Zone, joined by route tables.

boxes.label: Internet Gateway
boxes.says: The Internet Gateway connects the VPC to the internet.
boxes.detail: Public subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 to it. Only resources with public addresses are reachable through it.

boxes.label: NAT Gateway
boxes.says: NAT lets private instances reach out.
boxes.detail: Private subnets route to it for updates and APIs. It allows outbound connections only, never inbound.

boxes.label: VPC Endpoints
boxes.says: Endpoints reach AWS services without the internet.
boxes.detail: A gateway endpoint serves S3 and DynamoDB; interface endpoints put a private address in your subnet for other services.

boxes.label: PrivateLink
boxes.says: PrivateLink exposes a service privately.
boxes.detail: A provider publishes an endpoint service behind an NLB; consumers connect through an interface endpoint with no peering.

boxes.label: Route 53
boxes.says: Route 53 resolves the domain name.
boxes.detail: Managed DNS with health checks. Alias records point names at CloudFront, load balancers and S3.

boxes.label: CloudFront
boxes.says: CloudFront caches content near users.
boxes.detail: A content delivery network of edge locations. It caches responses and forwards misses to an origin such as an ALB or S3.

boxes.label: API Gateway
boxes.says: API Gateway is a managed API front door.
boxes.detail: Handles authentication, throttling and routing for REST and HTTP APIs. A VPC link reaches private backends.

boxes.label: ALB
boxes.says: ALB routes HTTP by host and path.
boxes.detail: Layer 7: terminates TLS with ACM and spreads requests across healthy targets by path or host rules.

boxes.label: NLB
boxes.says: NLB forwards TCP and UDP fast.
boxes.detail: Layer 4: very high throughput, low latency and static addresses. Also the front of a PrivateLink service.

boxes.label: Users
boxes.says: People reach the service over the internet.
boxes.detail: Browsers and clients resolve a name and connect over HTTPS.

boxes.label: Transit Gateway
boxes.says: Transit Gateway is a hub for many networks.
boxes.detail: Attach VPCs and on-premises links once; route tables decide who reaches whom. Avoids a mesh of peerings.

boxes.label: VPC Peering
boxes.says: Peering joins two VPCs directly.
boxes.detail: A one-to-one private route between two VPCs. Address ranges must not overlap and it is not transitive.

boxes.label: Other VPC
boxes.says: Another VPC or on-premises network.
boxes.detail: A second VPC, account or data centre joined through peering, Transit Gateway or a VPN.

steps.title: Resolve
steps.text: Route 53 answers the name and sends users to CloudFront.

steps.title: Balance
steps.text: CloudFront reaches the ALB; the ALB and NLB forward to EKS.

steps.title: Egress
steps.text: Pods leave through NAT, then the Internet Gateway.

steps.title: Private
steps.text: Endpoints and PrivateLink skip the internet.

steps.title: Connect
steps.text: Transit Gateway and peering join other networks.
